newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rises on weekend cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power rises on weekend cold.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. rose Thursday on outlook of cold weather arriving this weekend, and staying into the region at least through middle of next week.
"It looks like cooler weather pushed it up," said a Houston trader.

Firm spot natural gas prices also supported power prices on the same weather forecasts. Swing natgas at utilities' receipt points in New York City held steady in the $2.85-$2.90 per million British thermal units.
But the price increase was kept in check with several nuclear power plants in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
The 610 megawatt (MW) Oyster Creek nuclear power plant in Forked River, N.J., was scheduled to be placed on line some time today following its autumn refueling outage.

The 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit in Berwick, Pa., was holding at 75 percent of capacity amid work on a reactor feed pump. The unit was shut Oct 28 to replace a section of a steam drain pipe.
The 1,031 MW Hope Creek nuclear plant in Salem, N.J., was expected to resume operation this weekend after being shut less than a week ago for maintenance.

Transmission constraint from western to eastern part of the PJM district re-emerged as a concern due to reduced operation at Whitpain substation. The facility, north of Philadelphia., was damaged by a fire in early October.

Firm, peak PJM electricity for Friday was quoted in the $23.50-$24.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, with most deals heard done at $24.00 with a few reportedly changed hands as high as $25.00. Today's quote were lower than Wednesday's $23.00-$23.50.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for next-day delivery was again pegged at $14.00-$15.00, higher than Wednesday's quote.
PJM power deliveries for next week were valued at $25.25-$25.75.
For the balance of November, PJM electricity for firm, peak delivery was assessed at $25.00-$25.90, up from a range $24.00-$25.00 on Wednesday.
December PJM power with similar delivery conditions was discussed between $28.15 and $28.30, compared with Wednesday's $28.20-$28.40 range.
January/February 1997 PJM deliveries were valued slightly below Wednesday at $32.15-$32.30.
March 1997 PJM electricity climbed to $24.50-$24.80, up slightly from Wednesday's $24.25-$24.75.
July/August 1997 PJM power was notationally talked at $31.60-$31.85, down from Wednesday's quote of $32.00.
